- I did not rerun tests; this review is based on the live PR diff, linked issue context, and the PR’s declared verification.

This is explicitly deferred to a later slice, so it is not blocking for this PR’s stated scope, but it remains a rubric gap.

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #180 implements the `self-approval-core` slice from issue #175, which is part of the staged self-approval plan in parent issue #170.
- The PR adds `AGENT_ALLOW_SELF_APPROVE`, a manual `agent-self-approve` workflow, structured approval-agent parsing, deterministic resolve logic, docs, and focused tests.
- The intended safety model is opt-in, PR-only, open-state checked, trusted current-head `SHIP` review provenance, read-only agent inspection, and deterministic approval submission.
- Orchestration integration, status-comment upsert, and broader operational failure handling are explicitly deferred to later slices.

## Review
The implementation is well-scoped and most safety invariants are in place, but one approval-authority issue likely makes the feature fail in the default Sepo setup. The PR needs a branch change before it should ship.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Approval may be submitted by the PR author | BLOCKING | The workflow passes the normal Sepo auth token into the resolver for the `APPROVE` write, but Sepo-created PRs are authored by the same app actor in the default setup. GitHub does not allow pull request authors to approve their own PRs, so this path needs a distinct approval actor or a deterministic preflight/block. |
| Prepare success output contract lacks CLI coverage | WARNING | `prepare-self-approve` CLI tests cover stop paths, but not the success path that emits `should_run=true` and `head_sha`. A regression there would silently skip the approval-agent workflow branch. |

## Progress
- Rubrics review passed overall and acknowledged status-comment upsert plus broader failure visibility as intentionally deferred follow-up slices.
- Reviewer verification reported `npm ci`, `npm run build`, and focused `node --test` coverage passing, with only the existing Node engine warning.
- Existing inline PR comments were empty before mutation.
- Posted one inline comment on `.github/workflows/agent-self-approve.yml` line 137 for the approval-token issue; no replies or minimizations were made.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>Approval may be submitted by the PR author</summary>

**Cause:** `.github/workflows/agent-self-approve.yml` passes `steps.auth.outputs.token` to `resolve-self-approve`, and `.agent/src/cli/resolve-self-approve.ts` submits the `APPROVE` review with that token. In the public default setup, Sepo PRs are authored by `app/sepo-agent-app`, and the resolved auth token can be the same app actor. GitHub’s required-review docs state that pull request authors cannot approve their own pull requests: https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/approving-a-pull-request-with-required-reviews

**Candidate solutions:** Wire a distinct self-approval token/actor, or fetch both PR author and approval-token actor and block before submission when they normalize to the same actor. Add focused tests for same-author blocking and distinct-author approval.

**Comments:** One reviewer marked this blocking; the other reviews did not identify it, but there is no substantive disagreement on the underlying GitHub rule.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Prepare success output contract lacks CLI coverage</summary>

**Cause:** `.agent/src/__tests__/prepare-self-approve-cli.test.ts` currently covers disabled, non-PR, and closed-PR stop paths only. It does not exercise the successful open-PR plus trusted-current-head-`SHIP` provenance path.

**Candidate solutions:** Add a fake-`gh` integration test that returns an open PR and trusted synthesis comment, then assert `should_run=true`, `head_sha=<expected>`, and an empty/benign stop body output.

**Comments:** Core provenance logic and resolver approval flow have coverage, so this is a workflow contract gap rather than evidence of a current behavior bug.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
`FIX_PR`: Resolve the approval-author/token preflight and add focused CLI coverage; both are concrete branch changes that automation can make.

## Final Verdict
NEEDS_REWORK

- [ ] Add a `prepare-self-approve` CLI success-path test for `should_run=true` and `head_sha` output.

## Notes

- The requested success-path coverage was added: `prepare-self-approve` now has a trusted current-head `SHIP` test asserting `should_run=true` and `head_sha`.
- Remaining rubric gaps are aligned with the staged plan in #170: idempotent status upsert and broader workflow failure visibility are intentionally PR 4 work, not part of this core slice.

## Findings

- **INFO:** Resolver-level failures are visible, but failures before the resolver step, such as provider/runtime/agent step failures, still depend on later workflow polish for guaranteed visible status.

> @sepo-agent /answer left comments in the review 

@sepo-agent /answer check again

Checked again.

- Keep `agent-self-approve` on `approve-reads`. The self-approval agent is only the judgment layer; it returns JSON. The privileged PR approval write is owned by deterministic resolver code in [`resolve-self-approve.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/e7d2724ff8e0615104db9c022a56fd5ebe0b9afc/.agent/src/cli/resolve-self-approve.ts), after current-head, provenance, and actor checks. Using `approve-all` would widen agent tool authority without being needed.

- “Allow merging” should still map to a real GitHub `APPROVE` review when branch protection requires approvals. Sepo should not bypass that concept with a separate merge-allow signal. For non-approval, this PR records `REQUEST_CHANGES` as a self-approval conclusion/status, not a direct GitHub `REQUEST_CHANGES` review.

- This PR does not wire handback to the orchestrator. That is intentionally the next slice from parent #170, and is implemented in PR #184: `REQUEST_CHANGES` hands to `fix-pr`; terminal `approved` / `blocked` / `failed` results hand back for parent reporting.

- The workflow should leave a visible terminal signal. In this PR, approved runs leave the GitHub approval review body; non-approved/preflight stops post a status comment. The “always()/upsert/idempotent status” hardening is intentionally PR #186 operational polish.

So for PR #180 specifically, I do not see a required branch change from these comments. They are either intentional safety boundaries for this slice or covered by later stacked PRs (#184/#186).
